newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: ComTrade sole Ericsson mobile distributor in Yugo.
newsitem.headline: ComTrade sole Ericsson mobile distributor in Yugo.

text.p: Serbia's computer retailer ComTrade Group of Belgrade on Wednesday signed an agreement with Swedish telecom group Ericsson on sole distributorship of Ericsson mobile telephones in Yugoslavia.

"ComTrade has become Ericsson's exclusive representative for Yugoslavia, which now gets an official, authorised channel for organized sale of mobile phones," ComTrade Group President Veselin Jevrosimovic told Reuters.
Ericsson will enable ComTrade to provide after-sales support, servicing and distribution of new models in Yugoslavia.

"As one of the leading producers in the world, it was quite natural to combine that advantage with a leading distributor company in Yugoslavia," Jan Hultgren, General Manager of Ericsson Representative Office in Belgrade, told reporters.
The latest GSM phase 2 mobile phones will be offered through ComTrade's network of over 400 dealers in the country at competitive prices starting from 1,999 dinars ($345).
According to unofficial data, Ericsson mobile phones currently have 50 percent of the Yugoslav market.
"The joint work that we are presenting today is the beginning of long-term cooperation which will make mobile phones more readily available to buyers on the Yugoslav market," Jevrosimovic said.
